\begin{document}

\title{Memory-Efficient Explainable Pneumonia Detection Using a Quantized
EfficientNet-B0 for Resource-Constrained Healthcare Environments}

\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Sajan}
\IEEEauthorblockA{[Department]\\ [University]\\ sajankhad2@gmail.com}}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Pneumonia screening from chest X-rays (CXR) is valuable in low-resource settings, but
high-capacity models are memory-heavy and opaque. We present a reproducible,
deployment-honest framework combining a lightweight EfficientNet-B0 backbone,
integrated Grad-CAM++ explanations, and post-training INT8 quantization (dynamic and
static PTQ), with rigorous statistical and \emph{memory} reporting. Under an identical
pipeline against ResNet-18 and MobileNetV3-Small baselines, EfficientNet-B0 attains, on
the held-out Kermany test set ($n{=}624$), a ROC-AUC of \textbf{0.968} (95\% CI
0.950--0.982), sensitivity 0.967, specificity 0.838, and F1 0.937, with the best
precision/specificity balance of the three models. An automated integrity check
detected and removed \textbf{26 duplicate images} causing train--validation leakage.
\textbf{Static INT8} quantization compresses the model \textbf{70.5\%} (17.7$\rightarrow$5.2~MB),
speeds CPU inference \textbf{$\sim$8$\times$} (133$\rightarrow$16~ms), and cuts
\textbf{inference-time memory increase $\sim$30$\times$} (1156$\rightarrow$39~MB, median
of 5 isolated runs) for a 2.3-point AUC cost, while a lazy streaming data pipeline uses
\textbf{$\sim$10.5$\times$ less RAM} than naïve full-dataset loading. All code,
configurations, tests, and artifacts
are released; no result is simulated.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
pneumonia detection, chest X-ray, EfficientNet, Grad-CAM++, INT8 quantization, memory
efficiency, edge AI, explainable AI, reproducible research
\end{IEEEkeywords}

\section{Introduction}
Pneumonia is a leading cause of childhood mortality, with the greatest burden in
low- and middle-income countries where expert CXR interpretation is scarce. Deep
learning can assist screening, but deployment is limited by memory and compute cost
and by model opacity. Lightweight backbones already reach $\sim$95\% F1 on public
pediatric CXR data~\cite{benmalek2025,pneunet2026}, so the open problem is not
\emph{whether} a small model works but \emph{how honestly it is evaluated and how
efficiently it can be deployed}. Our contributions are: (1) an integrated, reproducible
pipeline (three backbones, identical protocol) with confidence intervals; (2) an
automatic data-integrity check that quantifies and removes train/validation leakage;
(3) a transparent dynamic-vs-static INT8 quantization study, including the practical
finding that per-channel weight quantization is required to keep EfficientNet-B0 from
collapsing; and (4) a correct memory-footprint analysis (peak RSS, not
\texttt{tracemalloc}) covering both the data pipeline and per-precision inference.

\section{Related Work}
CheXNet~\cite{rajpurkar2017} established CNN CXR classification but is parameter- and
memory-heavy. Lightweight backbones (EfficientNet~\cite{tan2019}) and edge studies on
pediatric pneumonia~\cite{benmalek2025,pneunet2026} achieve comparable accuracy at a
fraction of the cost; however, these report accuracy/F1 alone, without confidence
intervals, leakage control, a quantization-scheme comparison, or memory analysis.
Grad-CAM++~\cite{chattopadhay2018} provides saliency explanations, but saliency methods
must be validated rather than assumed~\cite{saporta2022}; we therefore treat
explanations as qualitative. Post-training quantization~\cite{jacob2018} reduces size
and latency; we additionally measure its effect on \emph{memory}.

\section{Methodology}
\subsection{Dataset, Integrity, and Splits}
Kermany pediatric CXR~\cite{kermany2018} (train 5{,}216; test 624). A stratified 20\%
validation split is carved from train and the official test set is held out. An
automatic check (MD5 duplicates; path/content leakage) found 16 within-train duplicate
groups and 9 train--validation content leaks; deduplicating the train pool (26 files)
makes the splits content-disjoint while the test set stays canonical.
\input{../results/tables/table1_dataset_statistics.tex}

\subsection{Model and Training}
EfficientNet-B0 with a shared binary head (BN--Dropout--Linear--ReLU--Dropout--Linear);
staged freeze/unfreeze transfer learning; AdamW, 3-epoch warmup + cosine schedule,
label smoothing, early stopping on validation AUC. The identical pipeline trains
ResNet-18 and MobileNetV3-Small.
\input{../results/tables/table2_training_config.tex}

\subsection{Evaluation, Quantization, and Benchmarking}
We report accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1, and ROC-AUC with bootstrap 95\% CIs
(1{,}000 resamples) and the Youden-J operating point. We compare dynamic and static
INT8 PTQ (FX graph mode, per-channel symmetric weights, histogram activation observers,
calibrated on clean validation data; \texttt{qnnpack} backend). Efficiency is measured
as on-disk size, warmup-corrected latency, throughput, and peak process RSS.

\section{Results}
\subsection{Diagnostic Performance and Baselines}
EfficientNet-B0 reaches test ROC-AUC 0.968 (95\% CI 0.950--0.982), sensitivity 0.967,
specificity 0.838, F1 0.937 (Table~\ref{tab:final}). All three backbones exceed 0.95
AUC; MobileNetV3-Small has the highest AUC (0.974) at the smallest size (4.4~MB), but
the baselines over-predict pneumonia (72 and 77 false positives vs.\ 38 for
EfficientNet-B0), so EfficientNet-B0 gives the best precision/specificity balance
(Table~\ref{tab:models}). At the Youden threshold (0.918) specificity rises to 0.919.

\subsection{Quantization, Efficiency, and Memory}
Dynamic INT8 preserves AUC ($-0.04\%$) but compresses only $\sim$6\%; static INT8 PTQ
compresses 70.5\% (17.7$\rightarrow$5.2~MB), is $\sim$8$\times$ faster on CPU
(133$\rightarrow$16~ms), and reduces the inference-time memory increase $\sim$30$\times$
(1156$\rightarrow$39~MB, median of 5 isolated runs) for a 2.34-point AUC cost
(Tables~\ref{tab:quant}, \ref{tab:efficiency}). The lazy streaming loader uses
$\sim$10.5$\times$ less RAM than
loading the dataset into memory (336~MB vs.\ 3{,}141~MB). The backend-default
per-tensor configuration collapses EfficientNet-B0 (AUC~$\approx$0.40); per-channel
weights recover it.

\subsection{Explainability}
\begin{figure}[t]\centering
  \includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{efficientnet_b0_gradcam_grid.png}
  \caption{Grad-CAM++ overlays for correct, false-positive, false-negative cases.}
  \label{fig:gradcam}
\end{figure}
Grad-CAM++ overlays (correct/FP/FN) concentrate on opacified lung regions for true
positives; false negatives are low-probability, subtle cases. Explanations are
qualitative; clinician validation is future work.

\section{Discussion}
All evaluated lightweight backbones are accurate on this task; the contribution is
\emph{rigour}: leakage control, confidence intervals, a quantization-scheme comparison,
and memory measurement. Static INT8 is the recommended deployment configuration --- it
cuts both storage and runtime memory several-fold at a small, threshold-recoverable
accuracy cost --- with per-channel quantization as a necessary detail for
EfficientNet-class models. The system is positioned as screening/decision support, with
the operating point a deployment parameter.

\section{Limitations and Future Work}
Single (pediatric, single-institution) dataset; no clinical-reader or
on-device-hardware validation (none simulated); class imbalance. The primary result is
corroborated by 5-fold cross-validation (mean AUC 0.971, std 0.006, each fold evaluated
on the same held-out test set), but this was not repeated for the baseline
architectures, and fold assignment is image-level rather than confirmed patient-level.
Future work: external
validation (NIH ChestX-ray14, CheXpert), quantization-aware training to close the PTQ
gap, on-device (Raspberry Pi / Jetson) benchmarking, and quantitative explanation
evaluation against bounding boxes (e.g., RSNA).

\section{Conclusion}
A quantized, explainable EfficientNet-B0 delivers ROC-AUC 0.968 on held-out Kermany CXR
while operating within a small, predictable memory budget (5.2~MB model, 39~MB
inference-time RAM increase) --- shown through honest, reproducible measurement. Code and artifacts
are released.
